title: Boss: config and data
summary: Three configuration tickets on a real Kubernetes cluster: missing references, a quota, and a Kustomize overlay for production.

steps.title: The scene
body: Configuration tickets, each on its own one-node **Kubernetes 1.37** cluster: a release whose pods never start, a
team namespace out of quota, and the production overlay nobody wrote. Use `kubectl describe`, `kubectl get events`,

steps.title: Ticket 1: CreateContainerConfigError
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`). The new `billing` release never starts: `kubectl get pods` shows `CreateContainerConfigError`.
`kubectl describe pod` says what is missing. Provide what it needs (the invoice prefix is `INV`, and the payment key
for this test cluster is `sk_test_example_123`) without changing the Deployment, so that the pod runs and logs

checks.name: billing runs
checks.cmd: kubectl rollout status deploy/billing --timeout=40s >/dev/null && kubectl logs $(kubectl get pods -l app=billing -o json | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.metadata.deletionTimestamp == null)] | sort_by(.metadata.creationTimestamp) | last | .metadata.name')
checks.expectOutput: billing: INV invoices in EUR (key of 19 characters)
checks.fail: `billing` is not running yet (or logs something else). `kubectl describe pod -l app=billing` shows the missing reference.

checks.name: the key is in a Secret, not a ConfigMap
checks.cmd: kubectl get secret billing-secrets -o jsonpath='{.data.stripe-key}' | base64 -d
checks.fail: Create the Secret `billing-secrets` with the key `stripe-key`.

checks.name: the Deployment is unchanged
checks.fail: Fix the references' targets, not the Deployment.

hints: `kubectl describe pod -l app=billing | tail` names the first missing piece; fix it and look again for the next.
One key is missing from the ConfigMap `billing-config`, and the Secret `billing-secrets` does not exist.
`kubectl patch configmap billing-config -p '{"data":{"INVOICE_PREFIX":"INV"}}'` and `kubectl create secret generic billing-secrets --from-literal=stripe-key=sk_test_example_123`.
steps.explain: `CreateContainerConfigError` means the kubelet could not build the container's environment or volumes: a missing ConfigMap, Secret, or key. The kubelet keeps retrying, so creating the missing pieces is enough; no restart needed. `optional: true` on a reference turns a hard failure into an empty value, which is only right for truly optional settings.

steps.title: Ticket 2: the team is out of quota
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`). In the namespace `reports`, the `renderer` Deployment wants 3 replicas but only some pods exist.
`kubectl get rs -n reports` and `kubectl describe quota -n reports` show why. The quota is the team's budget and stays
as it is. Change `renderer`'s resources so that all **3** replicas run **within** the quota, with each pod still
requesting at least `250m` CPU and `256Mi` memory.

checks.name: 3 renderer pods are ready
checks.cmd: kubectl -n reports rollout status deploy/renderer --timeout=40s >/dev/null; kubectl -n reports get deploy renderer -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}'
checks.fail: Not all 3 replicas run. The quota rejects pods whose requests (or limits) would exceed it.

checks.name: each pod requests at least 250m and 256Mi
checks.cmd: kubectl -n reports get deploy renderer -o json | jq -r '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources.requests | "\(.cpu) \(.memory)"'
checks.fail: Keep requests of at least `250m` CPU and `256Mi` memory.

checks.name: the quota is unchanged
checks.cmd: kubectl -n reports get resourcequota team-quota -o jsonpath='{.spec.hard.requests\.cpu} {.spec.hard.requests\.memory} {.spec.hard.limits\.memory}'

hints: `kubectl get events -n reports --field-selector reason=FailedCreate` quotes the quota error: which resource, used and limited.

Three pods must fit in `requests.cpu: 1`, `requests.memory: 1Gi` and `limits.memory: 2Gi` together. And a rolling update needs room for **new** pods while the old ones still count against the quota: here it never has any, so the rollout deadlocks. Replace the old pods first (`strategy: Recreate`), or scale to 0 and back.

`kubectl -n reports patch deploy renderer -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"type":"Recreate","rollingUpdate":null}}}'`, then `kubectl -n reports set resources deploy renderer --requests=cpu=300m,memory=300Mi --limits=memory=600Mi`.
solution: kubectl -n reports get events --field-selector reason=FailedCreate | tail -n 2
kubectl -n reports set resources deploy renderer --requests=cpu=300m,memory=300Mi --limits=memory=600Mi
steps.explain: A ResourceQuota is enforced at admission: the ReplicaSet's pod creations are rejected (`FailedCreate`, visible on the ReplicaSet and in events), so the pods never even reach `Pending`. Quantities add up across the namespace: `500m × 3` is more than `1` CPU. Teams usually pair a quota with a `LimitRange` so pods without requests get sane defaults instead of being rejected.

steps.title: Ticket 3: write the production overlay
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`). `~/deploy/base` is a Kustomize base for the API (`kubectl kustomize ~/deploy/base` renders it). Write
the production overlay in `~/deploy/overlays/prod` and apply it with `kubectl apply -k` so that, in the namespace
2. its config says `LOG_LEVEL=warn` and `ENVIRONMENT=prod` (the base's generated ConfigMap, overridden);
Do not edit the base: dev uses it as it is.

checks.name: api runs 3 replicas in prod
checks.cmd: kubectl -n prod rollout status deploy/api --timeout=40s >/dev/null; kubectl -n prod get deploy api -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}'
checks.fail: There should be 3 ready `api` pods in `prod`. `kubectl apply -k ~/deploy/overlays/prod`.

checks.name: the prod config reached the pods
checks.cmd: kubectl -n prod logs $(kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=api -o json | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.metadata.deletionTimestamp == null)] | sort_by(.metadata.creationTimestamp) | last | .metadata.name')
checks.expectOutput: api: log level warn in prod
checks.fail: The pods do not log `log level warn in prod`: override the base's `configMapGenerator`.

checks.name: everything is labelled env=prod
checks.cmd: kubectl -n prod get deploy,configmap -l env=prod -o name | grep -c -E 'deployment|configmap/api-config'

checks.name: the base is unchanged
checks.fail: Leave the base as it is.

hints: The overlay's `kustomization.yaml`: `resources: [../../base]`, `namespace: prod`, and the changes on top.
`replicas: [{name: api, count: 3}]`; `configMapGenerator: [{name: api-config, behavior: merge, literals: [LOG_LEVEL=warn, ENVIRONMENT=prod]}]`.
`labels: [{pairs: {env: prod}, includeSelectors: false}]`; check with `kubectl kustomize ~/deploy/overlays/prod` before `kubectl apply -k`.
steps.explain: Kustomize is built into `kubectl` (`-k`), and base plus overlays is the common way to keep one set of manifests for every environment. Note the generated ConfigMap's name, `api-config-<hash>`: the hash changes whenever the content does, and the Deployment's reference is rewritten to match, so a config change rolls the pods automatically. That is the problem the old "render a template" approach never solved.
